title: Testing finite Tor amplitude at the residue field
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $n\geq1$, put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$, and let $T$ be a scheme. Write $A_T,\kappa_T$ for the constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on the small etale site of $T$. Let $K\in D(T_{\Et},A)$ in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] have bounded constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. For integers $a,b$, $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude] if and only if
$$
\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^L\kappa_T)=0\qquad(i\notin[a,b]),
$$
where derived tensor is the etale construction [def-kun-derived-tensor].

proof.text: By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $\mathcal O_E$ has maximal ideal $(\varpi_E)$ and finite residue field. By [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], $A$ is finite local with maximal ideal $(\varpi_E)/(\varpi_E^n)$. Thus $\kappa$ is the field $\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E)$, and $\varpi_E^n=0$ in $A$. The constant-sheaf construction [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and exactness of sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], applied to the constant-presheaf sequence $A\xrightarrow{\varpi_E}A\to\kappa\to0$, identify $A_T/\varpi_E A_T$ with $\kappa_T$. A sheaf of $A_T$-modules killed by $\varpi_E$ therefore has a unique $\kappa_T$-module structure: locally write a section of the quotient ring as the image of a section of $A_T$ and let it act using that lift; different lifts differ by $\varpi_E A_T$ and act identically.
If $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, take $\mathcal M=\kappa_T$ in the definition [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. This gives exactly the asserted cohomology vanishing.

Conversely assume the asserted vanishing. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the ringed site $(T_{\Et},A_T)$ to a representative of $K$, obtaining a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with every term $P^q$ flat. By [def-kun-derived-tensor], for any $A_T$-module sheaf $M$ in degree zero, $P\otimes_{A_T}M$ represents $K\otimes_A^L M$. Put $C=P\otimes_{A_T}\kappa_T$, a complex of $\kappa_T$-modules. The hypothesis says $\mathcal H^i(C)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. No boundedness of $P$ or $C$ is assumed.

Let $N$ be any $\kappa_T$-module sheaf. By step 1, $\kappa$ is a field and $\kappa_T$ is its constant sheaf of rings on $T_{\Et}$; apply [lem-exc-constant-field-sheaf-tensor-cohomology] to the complex $C$ of $\kappa_T$-modules from step 3 and to $N$. It gives
$$\mathcal H^i(C\otimes_{\kappa_T}N)\simeq\mathcal H^i(C)\otimes_{\kappa_T}N,$$
which vanishes for $i\notin[a,b]$ by step 3. Next compare with $P\otimes_{A_T}N$, where $N$ is an $A_T$-module through $A_T\to\kappa_T$. The formulas $(x\otimes t)\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes ty$ and $x\otimes y\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes y$ are balanced over the indicated rings and commute with restrictions and differentials. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] and the definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], each sheaf tensor product is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor, so local sections are locally sums of pure tensors; the formulas define maps on these generators, balancing makes them independent of representatives, and sheafification glues them. Both composites fix every pure tensor, hence every local section. This gives an isomorphism of complexes
$$(P\otimes_{A_T}\kappa_T)\otimes_{\kappa_T}N\simeq P\otimes_{A_T}N.$$
Thus $\mathcal H^i(P\otimes_{A_T}N)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$.

source.place: Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor, and Section 03EK (tensor product) for the change-of-rings comparison; the field calculation is the new node lem-exc-constant-field-sheaf-tensor-cohomology

proof.text: For an arbitrary $A_T$-module sheaf $M$ put $F_sM=\operatorname{im}(\varpi_E^s:M\to M)$, $0\leq s\leq n$. Then $F_0M=M$ and $F_nM=0$. Write $G_s=F_sM/F_{s+1}M$. Multiplication by $\varpi_E$ sends $F_sM$ into $F_{s+1}M$: locally its section is $\varpi_E^s m$, and its product is $\varpi_E^{s+1}m$. Hence $G_s$ is killed by $\varpi_E$, so step 1 makes it a $\kappa_T$-module sheaf and step 4 applies to $G_s$. This is a finite filtration for every $M$, including sheaves without any finiteness or constructibility condition.

source.place: Elementary image/quotient filtration by powers of the scalar; coefficient quotient identified in step 1

proof.text:
For $0\leq s<n$, tensor the short exact sequence $0\to F_{s+1}M\to F_sM\to G_s\to0$ termwise with $P$. Each $P^q$ is flat, so [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], with the elementary symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$, gives a short exact sequence of complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact],
$$\mathcal H^i(P\otimes F_{s+1}M)\longrightarrow\mathcal H^i(P\otimes F_sM)\longrightarrow\mathcal H^i(P\otimes G_s)$$
is exact. Fix $i\notin[a,b]$. Descending induction on $s$ starts at $F_nM=0$. At the induction step the left group is zero by induction and the right group is zero by step 4, so the middle group is zero. At $s=0$ this proves $\mathcal H^i(P\otimes M)=0$. By [def-kun-derived-tensor] this is $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^L M)=0$. Since $M$ and $i\notin[a,b]$ were arbitrary, [def-kun-tor-amplitude] proves the converse with exactly the same interval.

split_report.summary: Audited the imported residue-field Tor criterion against the current main-20261015 blueprint and Stacks-based filtration proof. The statement keeps the explicit finite extension, level n, ordinary small-etale site, bounded constructibility, and exact interval. The six-step proof uses the nilpotent scalar filtration, K-flat resolution, sectionwise field tensor calculation, sheafification exactness, and long exact sequence; no new nodes are needed. Existing proof, dependencies, blueprint metadata, and prior review fields are retained; citations.json records verbatim statements for all cited nodes. Mathlib searches were run for this item and found no direct match. Review repair (Q64 cc reviewer, 2026-10-17): the sectionwise field-tensor calculation formerly proved inside step 4 is a separate site-general lemma and is now the statement-only node lem-exc-constant-field-sheaf-tensor-cohomology, which step 4 cites.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the forward implication of the first paragraph and the uniform sheafwise converse of the second paragraph of lem-exc-residue-tor-test, Proof. Below the unchanged unit sk-prop-sf-trace-perfectness (which has no proof steps), the minimal-resolution and stalk calculation is replaced by the written scalar filtration and sectionwise field calculation.
